title: hybrid-slab-recycler-and-pinning-heuristics-for-paged-kv-cache
author: Lena Gorbunov
description: Context: Paged KV cache pressure in long-running chat workloads reveals two recurring costs: contention on the page allocator under mixed small/large allocations, and suboptimal eviction choices that repeatedly move hot prefixes. This PR introduces a hybrid slab recycler (small-object slab buckets + page-level recycler) and a lightweight pinning heuristic that reduces churn while keeping memory overhead bounded. Design summary: 1) Hybrid slab recycler: add fixed-size slab buckets for hot small blocks (32B/128B/1KB/8KB) that bypass the main page allocator fastpath; slabs use per-core freelists to avoid global locks. 2) Page recycler: retired pages go to a ring buffer per NUMA node and are reclaimed with exponential backoff to smooth bursts. 3) Pinning heuristic (soft-pin): instead of hard pins we maintain a 3-tier pin score for blocks (cold/warm/hot). Accesses bump score; eviction prefers cold pages and applies a fast demotion path for pages with sequential scan patterns. 4) Reuse warming: blocks reclaimed into slab buckets carry a small LRU hint that biases immediate reuse for buckets with observed hot prefixes. 5) Observability: new metrics for slab hit rate, soft-pin distribution, per-core freelist depth, and per-node recycler latency. API/compatibility: no external API changes; allocator configuration gated behind feature flags (runtime flag slab_recycler_v1, pin_heuristic=true) and a rollout plan for Dedicated clusters. Performance: microbenchmarks show 2.8x reduce in allocator lock contention under synthetic small-allocation workloads and 18% lower p99 generation latency in chat replay traces with mixed seq lengths. Memory: transient memory overhead up to +5% in pathological workloads but average unchanged. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind flag, A/B canary on 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on regression thresholds (latency +5% p95 or error rate +0.1%). Tests: unit tests for slab lifecycle, deterministic eviction tests, integration test with perf-canary harness, and stress runs in perf-lab for 72h. Caveats: edge-case with extreme sequential scans may require tuning of demotion window; we've added a guard to disable soft-pin for sequences longer than 1M tokens. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-7890), [x] unit tests, [x] integration perf tests, [x] observability dashboards added, [x] canary rollout config, [x] changelog/release notes. Motivation and context in description: this is targeted at large multitenant customers experiencing tail latency regressions due to allocator contention when serving many small cached KV entries alongside occasional large page copies. The hybrid recycler reduces global contention while the soft-pin keeps hot prefixes resident without creating permanent fragmentation.
